ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

distal radius — pattern 2

A 45-year-old man falls onto a flexed wrist. Radiographs show an extra-articular distal radial fracture with the distal fragment angulated toward the palm. There is no rim fragment carrying a subluxed carpus and no isolated styloid fracture. Which distal radius fracture pattern is described?

  1. Die-punch fracture
  2. Colles fracture
  3. Smith fracture
  4. Barton fracture
  5. Chauffeur fracture
Answer and explanation

Smith fracture

Smith fracture: An extra-articular distal radius fracture with volar displacement or angulation.

Option explanations

Smith fracture: Smith fracture: An extra-articular distal radius fracture with volar displacement or angulation.

Barton fracture: Barton fracture describes an intra-articular rim shear fracture with associated radiocarpal subluxation or dislocation. The case instead matches Smith fracture.

Chauffeur fracture: Chauffeur fracture describes an intra-articular fracture of the radial styloid. The case instead matches Smith fracture.

Die-punch fracture: Die-punch fracture describes an impacted depression of the distal radial lunate fossa. The case instead matches Smith fracture.

Colles fracture: Colles fracture describes an extra-articular distal radius fracture with dorsal displacement or angulation. The case instead matches Smith fracture.
